title: Structured CBT Protocol for Anxiety
implementation_guidance: Implement a structured cognitive-behavioral therapy protocol for anxiety that includes: 1) Conducting a comprehensive assessment using the GAD-7 and specific phobia scales as appropriate; 2) Providing psychoeducation on the cognitive-behavioral model of anxiety using personalized examples from the client's experience; 3) Teaching specific diaphragmatic breathing and progressive muscle relaxation techniques with in-session practice and daily homework assignments; 4) Implementing cognitive restructuring using thought records that identify and challenge specific anxiety-provoking thoughts; 5) Creating a graduated exposure hierarchy with subjective units of distress (SUDS) ratings for each feared situation; and 6) Conducting in-vivo or imaginal exposure exercises with specific pre/post SUDS measurements. The protocol should follow a 12-session structure with clearly defined goals for each session and homework assignments that build progressively.
expected_outcomes: Reduced anxiety symptoms as measured by standardized scales, decreased avoidance behaviors, improved daily functioning in previously avoided situations, enhanced self-efficacy in managing anxiety, and development of sustainable coping skills.
target_population: Adults with generalized anxiety disorder, social anxiety, specific phobias, or panic disorder
citation: Carpenter JK, Andrews LA, Witcraft SM, Powers MB, Smits JAJ, Hofmann SG. Cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety and related disorders: A meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials. Depress Anxiety. 2018;35(6):502-514. doi:10.1002/da.22728
